# Installing Your CLI Assistant

Before we can start building, we need to install the CLI you chose: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, or GitHub Copilot CLI. We recommend Homebrew for macOS because it keeps installs clean and easy to update. If you run into any issues during installation, you can ask a chat AI like ChatGPT or claude.ai---just describe the error you're seeing.

## Step 1: Confirm Your Choice

You should have picked a tool in the preface. As a reminder:

- **Claude Code** if you want a purpose-built coding CLI and already use Claude.
- **Codex CLI** if you already have OpenAI access to Codex.
- **Copilot CLI** if you already pay for GitHub Copilot.

:::{.callout-note}
## About Subscriptions
Each tool offers free and paid tiers. Free tiers work for light exploration, but you'll likely hit usage limits during active development. Expect to use a paid subscription ($20-30/month) for serious project work. If you hit a rate limit, your CLI will pause until the limit resets—your work isn't lost, you just wait.
:::

## Step 2: Install Homebrew

Homebrew is a package manager for macOS that makes installing and updating tools easy. Paste this into Terminal:

```bash
/bin/bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Homebrew/install/HEAD/install.sh)"
```

Follow the prompts. When it finishes, it may tell you to run a couple of commands to add Homebrew to your path—copy and run those if prompted.

For the latest instructions, visit [brew.sh](https://brew.sh).

:::{.callout-note}
If you can't use Homebrew, see the official docs for alternative install options:

- Claude Code: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/setup>
- Codex CLI: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/quickstart>
- Copilot CLI: <https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/set-up/install-copilot-cli>
:::

## Step 3: Install Your CLI

Run the install command for your chosen tool:

### Claude Code

```bash
brew install --cask claude-code
```

### OpenAI Codex CLI

```bash
brew install --cask codex
```

### GitHub Copilot CLI

```bash
brew install --cask copilot-cli
```

## Step 4: First Launch

Navigate to your project folder (from Chapter 2) and launch your CLI:

- Claude Code: `claude`
- Codex CLI: `codex`
- Copilot CLI: `copilot`

On first launch, you'll need to authenticate. Claude Code and Codex CLI will open a browser automatically. For Copilot CLI, type `/login` when prompted.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Example Prompt
"Help me verify that everything is installed correctly. Check that I have git available."
:::

If the tool can run a basic command and explain the result, you're ready to continue.

## Step 5: Learn the Basics

Each CLI has its own interactive workflow. Here are the basics you'll use most often.

### Claude Code

- `/help` to list available commands
- `/clear` to clear the current conversation
- `Esc` to cancel a response mid-generation
- `/exit` or `Ctrl+C` to quit
- `/resume` to continue a previous session

### OpenAI Codex CLI

- `/approvals` to change approval modes
- `/status` to see the current model and settings
- `/diff` to review changes before you commit
- `/exit` or `Ctrl+C` to quit

### GitHub Copilot CLI

- `/login` to authenticate (if needed)
- `?` or `copilot help` to see commands and options

## Next Steps

With your CLI installed and working, you're ready to start building. But first, let's make sure you understand the landscape---what a "tech stack" is and what the pieces of a modern application look like.
